label: UGC NET June 2026 Paper 2 — Official Statistics questions not in the 1–50 set (booklet numbers not known; identified by official question ID)

items.stem: Arrange the following statistical organizations in order of their year of establishment from oldest to latest. A. Central Statistics Office (CSO) B. National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) C. National Statistical Office (NSO) D. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI) E. National Statistical Commission (NSC) Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Recall the founding years and sort them. The NSSO came first (1950) and the CSO a year later (1951); the ministry (MoSPI) was formed in 1999, the National Statistical Commission in 2006, and the NSO in 2019 when the CSO and NSSO were merged into it. Working: NSSO 1950, CSO 1951, MoSPI 1999, NSC 2006, NSO 2019 -> B, A, D, E, C. Official answer: D (B, A, D, E, C).

items.stem: Match LIST-I with LIST-II. LIST-I: A. P. C. Mahalanobis; B. P. V. Sukhatme; C. R. C. Bose; D. S. N. Roy. LIST-II: I. Partially Balanced Incomplete Block Design (PBIBD); II. Multivariate hypothesis testing; III. Ordered estimates in sampling with varying probabilities and WOR; IV. Distance measure in multivariate analysis.
items.explanation: Idea: match the names you are sure of first: the Mahalanobis distance, Bose's PBIB designs and Roy's multivariate tests. The remaining pair then follows. Working: Mahalanobis distance (A-IV); Bose with Nair introduced PBIBDs (C-I); Roy's union–intersection multivariate tests (D-II); which leaves B-III for Sukhatme (sampling theory). Source note: Ordered estimators in PPS sampling without replacement are usually credited to Des Raj (and Murthy), not to P. V. Sukhatme. The official key follows from the other three matches by elimination. Official answer: C (A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II).
